questions.question: Dussehra festival is celebrated in which of the following Hindu months?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashwin**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dussehra** festival is celebrated in the Hindu month of **Ashwin**.
 
• It marks the victory of **Lord Rama** over the demon king **Ravana**.
 
• The festival signifies the triumph of **good over evil **and is celebrated with great enthusiasm across India.
 
• In some regions, it is also known as **Vijayadashami**.
 
• The celebration includes the burning of effigies of Ravana, symbolizing the destruction of evil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Hindu month of **Ashwin** typically falls in the Gregorian months of **September and October**.
 
• Dussehra is the culmination of the **Navratri festival**, which is a **nine-day celebration** dedicated to the worship of the **Goddess Durga**.
 
• It is one of the major festivals in India and is celebrated with various cultural performances, fairs, and processions.
 
• In some parts of India, people also celebrate the victory of Goddess Durga over the** buffalo demon Mahishasura**.
 
• Public celebrations include plays, dance dramas, and colorful processions depicting scenes from the Ramayana.

questions.question: Which country’s national game is Chinlone (Caneball)?
questions.solution:

• It is an integral part of Myanmar's culture and is often played during festivals and traditional events.

questions.question: What does SAARC stand for?

options.text: South Asian Association of Regional Climate change

__
 
• **South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation** (SAARC) is an organization of South Asian nations, established on **December 8, 1985**.
 
• SAARC aims to **promote economic and regional integration** among its member countries.
 
• The current member countries are **Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka**.
 
• The organization has its headquarters in **Kathmandu, Nepal**.
 
• SAARC's primary objectives include promoting the welfare of the peoples of South Asia and improving their quality of life, accelerating economic growth, social progress, and cultural development in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• SAARC was established with the signing of the **SAARC Charter in Dhaka, Bangladesh**.
 
• Since its inception, SAARC has conducted several summits aimed at addressing regional issues and fostering cooperation.
 
• SAARC also includes nine observer states: **Australia, China, the European Union, Iran, Japan, Mauritius, Myanmar, South Korea, and the United States**.
 
• Various regional centers have been established under the auspices of SAARC to promote regional cooperation in specific areas, such as the SAARC Disaster Management Centre and the SAARC Agricultural Centre.

questions.question: In February 2023, PARAKH became the First National Assessment Regulator. What does R stand for in PARAKH?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Review**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PARAKH** stands for **Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development**.
 
• In **February 2023**, PARAKH was established as the first national assessment regulator in India.
 
• The initiative aims to **standardize and improve the quality of assessments** across various educational boards in India.
 
• PARAKH will set norms, standards, and guidelines for student assessment and evaluation for all recognized school boards across the country.
 
• The regulator will also ensure the equivalence of academic standards among different boards, thereby promoting uniformity in assessments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The establishment of PARAKH is part of the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, which emphasizes the need for a holistic, multi-disciplinary approach to education.
 
• NEP 2020 aims to **transform India's education system by 2040**, making it more inclusive, flexible, and aligned with the needs of the 21st century.
 
• PARAKH will also play a crucial role in the assessment reforms proposed by NEP 2020, including competency-based assessment and reducing the emphasis on rote learning.
 
• The regulator will work towards creating a more balanced and integrated assessment system that evaluates students' understanding, skills, and competencies.

questions.question: The Atal Tunnel has been built by Border Road Organisation at an altitude of 3000 metres. Which places are connected by this tunnel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manali to Lahaul-Spiti**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Atal Tunnel** is a highway tunnel built under the **Rohtang Pass** in the **eastern Pir Panjal range of the Himalayas** on the** Leh-Manali Highway**.
 
• It connects **Manali to Lahaul-Spiti** valley throughout the year, which was previously cut off for about six months due to heavy snowfall.
 
• The tunnel is named after **former Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee** and is one of the **longest tunnels above 10,000 feet** in the world.
 
• The tunnel reduces the road distance between Manali and Leh by 46 kilometers and the time by about 4 to 5 hours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Atal Tunnel project was announced by Atal Bihari Vajpayee on June 3, 2000.
 
• The foundation stone for the access road to the south portal of the tunnel was laid on May 26, 2002.
 
• The tunnel was **inaugurated **by** Prime Minister Narendra Modi on October 3, 2020**.
 
• The tunnel is designed to handle traffic of up to 3,000 cars and 1,500 trucks per day.
 
• It is equipped with state-of-the-art electromechanical systems, including semi-transverse ventilation, SCADA-controlled firefighting, illumination, and monitoring systems.
 
• The tunnel also has an emergency escape tunnel built into the main tunnel itself.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act come into force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2015**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **100th Constitutional Amendment Act** came into force in the year **2015**.
 
• This amendment dealt with the** exchange of certain enclaves between India and Bangladesh**, resolving long-standing border issues between the two countries.
 
• The amendment aimed to formalize the transfer of territories and ensure better management and demarcation of the international boundary.
 
• It was a significant step in strengthening bilateral relations and cooperation between India and Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Constitution of India** was **adopted **by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect** on **26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the** longest written constitution** of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The** Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the** Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• **Amendments to the Constitution **can be made through a process outlined in** Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: Which Act was enacted by the British which regulated the manufacture, sale, possession and transport of firearms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Arms Act, 1878**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian Arms Act, 1878** was enacted by the **British to regulate the manufacture, sale, possession, and transport of firearms**.
 
• This Act was part of the colonial measures to **control arms and ammunition **among the Indian population.
 
• The Act required that Indians obtain licenses to possess, sell, or manufacture arms and ammunition.
 
• It was** aimed at preventing any potential uprising** or revolt by restricting access to weapons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indian Arms Act, 1878** was one of several laws enacted to maintain British control over India.
 
• The Act was repealed and replaced by the **Arms Act of 1959** post-Independence, which governs the current regulations related to arms and ammunition in India.
 
• The Arms Act of 1959 aims to curb illegal arms and ensure that firearms are used responsibly.
 
• Licenses for arms are now issued under the provisions of the 1959 Act, which includes various checks and balances to prevent misuse.

questions.question: Brihadiswara Temple of Tanjore was built by which of the following Chola emperors?

__
 
• **Raja Raja Chola** was the **Chola emperor** who built the **Brihadiswara Temple of Tanjore**.
 
• The Brihadiswara Temple, also known as **Peruvudaiyar Kovil**, is a Hindu temple dedicated to **Shiva **and is located in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• It is one of the largest temples in India and is an exemplary example of Dravidian architecture.
 
• The temple was built around 1010 AD and is a part of the** UNESCO World Heritage Site known as the "Great Living Chola Temples"**.
 
• Raja Raja Chola I was one of the greatest rulers of the Chola dynasty and his reign marked the peak of Chola power and influence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Raja Chola I** ruled between** 985 and 1014 AD** and expanded the Chola Empire to its zenith.
 
• The Brihadiswara Temple is renowned for its massive Vimana (temple tower) which is one of the tallest in the world.
 
• The temple complex includes a massive statue of Nandi (the sacred bull) and features intricate carvings and frescoes.
 
• Raja Raja Chola's contributions to art, architecture, and culture have left a lasting legacy in South India.
 
• The temple is still an active place of worship and attracts thousands of visitors and pilgrims every year.

questions.question: Which was the first programmable general purpose computer in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ENIAC**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer)** was the **first programmable general-purpose computer**.
 
• It was designed and built in the** United States during World War II**.
 
• ENIAC was capable of performing a wide variety of calculations, making it a versatile computing machine for its time.
 
• It was developed by** John Presper Eckert and John Mauchly** at the University of Pennsylvania.
 
• ENIAC was completed in 1945 and was used for calculations related to the development of the hydrogen bomb, weather prediction, cosmic ray studies, and other scientific applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ENIAC** was a groundbreaking machine that used** vacuum tubes for computation** and could **perform 5,000 additions per second**.
 
• It was a significant advancement over earlier mechanical computers, which were much slower and less reliable.
 
• The success of ENIAC demonstrated the potential of electronic computing and paved the way for the development of future computers.
 
• ENIAC's architecture and design principles influenced many subsequent computer designs.
 
• Despite its size and power consumption, ENIAC marked the beginning of the electronic computing era and had a profound impact on science, engineering, and technology.

questions.question: Electrochemical cell is a device which converts chemical energy into electrical energy in a/an _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**indirect redox reaction**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An electrochemical cell is a device that converts **chemical energy into electrical energy **through an **indirect redox reaction**.
 
• In an electrochemical cell, oxidation and reduction reactions occur in separate compartments, allowing the transfer of electrons through an external circuit.
 
• This separation of reactions helps in generating a potential difference that drives the flow of electrons, thus producing electrical energy.
 
• Examples of electrochemical cells include galvanic cells and batteries, which are widely used in various applications for power supply.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Redox reactions** involve the transfer of electrons between two species; **oxidation refers to the loss of electrons**, while** reduction refers to the gain of electrons**.
 
• In a **galvanic cell, the anode is the site of oxidation, and the cathode is the site of reduction**.
 
• The **electrolyte** in the cell facilitates the flow of ions, maintaining the charge balance as electrons move through the external circuit.
 
• Electrochemical cells are fundamental to the operation of batteries, fuel cells, and various types of sensors.

questions.question: Which of the following writs in Latin means ‘we command’?

__
 
• The writ of **Mandamus** in Latin means '**we command**'.
 
• It is** issued by a court to a public official, lower court, or government body to perform a duty they are obligated to complete**.
 
• Mandamus is one of the five writs under the Indian Constitution used to enforce the performance of public duties.
 
• This writ is a powerful tool to ensure that public authorities fulfil their duties as mandated by law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other writs include **Habeas Corpus, Certiorari, Prohibition,** and **Quo Warranto**.
 
• **Habeas Corpus** is used to bring a person who has been detained unlawfully to court.
 
• **Prohibition** is issued by a higher court to a lower court to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction.
 
• **Certiorari** is issued to transfer a case from a lower court to a higher court for review.
 
• **Quo Warranto** is issued to challenge the legality of a person's claim to a public office.
 
• These writs are essential for the protection of fundamental rights and the enforcement of the rule of law.
